body:
**36 issues found** across 53 files
Prompt for AI agents (unresolved issues) ```text Check if these issues are valid — if so, understand the root cause of each and fix them. When an issue isn't valid or won't be fixed in this PR, reply in its thread with the reason and then resolve the thread. If appropriate, use sub-agents to investigate and fix each issue separately. P2: This calculation can create an unsafe total even though the stored price is valid. With a `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` product and PPN 100%, `formatIDR(total)` throws during render instead of leaving the user with a checkout validation error; guard unsafe line/subtotal/tax totals before formatting and keep checkout usable. P2: These are journal-line rows, not transactions: repeating an account in one entry makes the header count report multiple transactions. Because `listLedger` has no within-entry line order, the per-line running balances can also vary; aggregate per entry or add deterministic line ordering before rendering. P2: This page fetches and renders every invoice for the organization with no limit or pagination. As invoice history grows, the query and RSC response become unbounded; add bounded pagination and a matching query path. P2: The org-isolation case covers only the expense account. Add a complementary request using an organization-A expense account and organization-B accumulated-depreciation account to verify both account fields are scoped. P2: This case does not test the two invalid inputs named in its comment. Add separate `salvageValue > cost` and `usefulLifeMonths: 0` calls so those validation paths cannot regress unnoticed. P2: This control is rendered for every journal member, but `closePeriod` requires admin, so members can open a close-period dialog that can never succeed. Gate the component with the membership role instead of rendering it unconditionally. P2: Closing this dialog without saving preserves both controlled account selections, so the next asset can be posted with the previous asset’s depreciation accounts. Reset both selections whenever `onOpenChange` receives `false`. P2: This admin-only action is rendered to every member on the asset page, causing a misleading form that always fails for non-admins. Pass the role into this component and hide the trigger for non-admin members. P2: This render scans the full posted ledger three times because `balanceSheet` recomputes `incomeStatement` after the page already requested it. Use a combined report service or share one trial-balance snapshot to avoid the repeated database and memory work. P2: The report page performs three full trial-balance scans for two panels because `balanceSheet` recomputes income internally. Use one combined report query or share a single trial-balance snapshot to avoid duplicate database work. P2: `balanced` ignores missing account selections, so the form displays “Seimbang — siap disimpan” for rows that the action removes before validation. Require every row to have an account and show a specific account-selection error before enabling submit. P2: The dialog enables and labels a draft ready when one or more rows still have no account. Require every row to select an account before setting `balanced`, and show an account-selection error instead of sending filtered rows that the server rejects. P2: The action accepts arbitrary date strings, but `createInvoice` compares them lexically. Validate and normalize both dates at this boundary, or make the service compare parsed calendar dates, so callers cannot create invoices with an earlier due date. P1: The service validates account ownership but not account type, so client-supplied IDs can misclassify depreciation postings. Load the accounts and require an expense account, an asset account, and distinct IDs on the server. P2: The period check accepts invalid months, causing silent no-ops for `MM=00` and database errors for `MM>12`. Restrict the month to `01`–`12` in both the server validation and the form pattern. P1: The asset snapshot is taken before the advisory lock, so concurrent runs can both post the same month; the second update affects zero rows but the code still increments `processed` and keeps its journal. Load or lock each asset inside the transaction, and only count it after a successful update. P0: The asset snapshot is read before the advisory lock, so concurrent runs can post duplicate depreciation journals from stale state; the failed expected-state update is ignored. Read and lock the active assets inside the transaction, and handle a zero-row update before creating the journal. P1: A positive depreciable base smaller than the useful life produces a zero monthly amount and is skipped forever, so the asset is never fully depreciated. Reject that combination or carry the rounding remainder across months instead of treating it as skippable. P2: Flooring every monthly installment leaves a remainder beyond the declared useful life for non-divisible bases. Post the rounding remainder in the final useful-life month rather than waiting for an extra month. P2: Depreciation journals are always dated on the 28th rather than the actual last day of `periodEnd`. Compute the last calendar day of the requested month so the journal date matches the documented period-end behavior. P1: Directly marking depreciation posted bypasses the fiscal-period close guard in `postEntry`, allowing depreciation to be added to a closed month. Check the period inside this transaction before inserting, or route posting through the same guard. P2: Full depreciation is being recorded as disposal, so fully depreciated assets without a disposal date are mislabeled and cannot later enter the disposal workflow. Keep depreciation completion separate from physical disposal, or add an explicit fully-depreciated state. P2: No production module imports this service, so budgeting cannot be reached by the application even though its integration tests pass. Wire these operations into a server action/page before shipping, or remove the dead service until it has a caller. P2: The period validation accepts nonexistent months such as `2026-13`, allowing invalid budgets and misleading zero-actual reports. Validate the month range (`01`–`12`) in all three service entry points and enforce the same calendar constraint in the database. P2: The `bigint` columns no longer enforce the engine’s 2^31−1 journal-line cap, allowing invoice and POS postings above that limit. Add an upper-bound CHECK or keep these columns `integer` so every journal writer shares the same constraint. P2: These foreign keys allow a tenant-scoped record to reference another organization’s account, invoice, company, contact, product, or sale. Enforce `(org_id, id)` ownership with composite unique keys and composite foreign keys (or equivalent database constraints) so a bad write cannot corrupt tenant isolation. P1: These audit calls use the global pool before the accounting transaction commits, so concurrent creates or posts can exhaust the five-connection pool and deadlock all requests. Make audit writes transaction-aware and execute them through `tx` (including the membership check). P2: The period guard accepts impossible months and lets them fail as raw database errors. Restrict the month to `01` through `12` before executing the close transaction. P2: A concurrent posting can produce a self-inconsistent balance sheet because its components come from different snapshots. Compute all report components from one transaction or repeatable-read snapshot. P2: `MAX_LINE_AMOUNT` still enforces the old PostgreSQL `integer` limit, so journal amounts above Rp2,147,483,647 are rejected despite `journal_lines` now being `bigint`. Use the JavaScript safe bound or document and enforce this as a separate business limit. P2: The balance helpers aggregate unbounded amounts with `number`, so cumulative postings can round past `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` and make balances or `balanced` incorrect. Accumulate with `BigInt` or reject an addition before it becomes unsafe. P2: `trialBalance` can report an unbalanced ledger as balanced after aggregate totals exceed `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, because unchecked JavaScript rounding makes distinct totals equal. Use exact integer aggregation or reject unsafe aggregates before returning the trial balance. P2: `trialBalance` silently classifies unmapped accounts as assets, producing the wrong normal balance for missing liability, equity, revenue, or expense metadata. Fail on a missing `types[accountCode]` instead of returning a fabricated classification. P2: The journal page limits entries to 50 but still loads every line in the organization. Filter lines by the selected entry IDs so page load and memory stay bounded as the ledger grows. P2: The journal displays raw account UUIDs instead of the account code or name. Join or map each line to its account so users can identify the accounts in the journal. P2: `postJournal` bypasses the accounting line cap, allowing large invoices to post journal lines above `MAX_LINE_AMOUNT`. Validate the generated lines or reject totals above the cap before inserting them. ```

Prompt for AI agents (unresolved issues) ```text Check if these issues are valid — if so, understand the root cause of each and fix them. When an issue isn't valid or won't be fixed in this PR, reply in its thread with the reason and then resolve the thread. If appropriate, use sub-agents to investigate and fix each issue separately. P3: This findings document repeats several issues as separate violations even though each pair has the same location, root cause, and fix. Consolidate the duplicate entries so agents do not investigate or track the same defect multiple times. P2: Validate `unitPrice` with the same digit-only rule as the server. This guard lets `1e3` and whitespace-wrapped numbers through because `Number(...)` yields 1000, while `parseIDRInput` rejects them, so the dialog shows totals but submission fails. P2: Guard the aggregate subtotal and tax-inclusive total before returning them. Otherwise two maximum-price items, or one maximum-price item with 100% PPN, make `formatIDR` throw during render and crash the invoice dialog instead of showing validation. P2: After saving, the reset clears items and company but not `taxPct`; the next invoice silently reuses the previous PPN instead of the initial 0%. Reset `taxPct` with the other form fields. P2: Reset draft state when the dialog closes, not only after a successful save. Clicking Batal, X, or Escape leaves `items`, `companyId`, and `taxPct` populated, so reopening displays the previous invoice and permits accidental resubmission. ```
